simple_explanation: If your 12V car battery is dead and won't turn on, you can jump-start it safely using jumper cables and a donor car with a healthy 12V battery.
step_by_step: 1. Park the helper car close to your Tata Punch without the cars touching. Turn off both engines and set handbrakes.
2. Connect the RED jumper cable clamp to the POSITIVE (+) terminal of your Tata Punch dead battery.
3. Connect the other end of the RED cable to the POSITIVE (+) terminal of the helper car's battery.
4. Connect the BLACK jumper cable clamp to the NEGATIVE (-) terminal of the helper car's battery.
5. Connect the other end of the BLACK cable to an unpainted metal bolt or engine bracket on your Tata Punch (keep away from the battery).
6. Start the helper car's engine and let it run for 3-5 minutes.
7. Start your Tata Punch. Once it starts, let both run for 3 minutes.
8. Remove cables in REVERSE order: Black from your car, Black from helper car, Red from helper car, Red from your car.
9. Drive your car for at least 20-30 minutes so the alternator can recharge your battery.

topic: Changing a Flat Tyre and Jacking Points
simple_explanation: If you get a flat tyre, pull over to a flat, safe surface, turn on hazard lights, and follow these easy steps using the spare wheel and jack in your boot.
step_by_step: 1. Park on firm, level ground, engage the handbrake firmly, and put the gear in 1st gear or Park.
2. Open the boot, lift the boot floor mat, and take out the jack, wheel spanner, and spare wheel.
3. Loosen the 4 wheel lug nuts with the spanner by turning counter-clockwise 1/2 turn (do not remove them yet).
4. Locate the reinforced jacking point slot under the car sill right behind the front wheel or ahead of the rear wheel.
5. Turn the jack screw clockwise by hand until it seats into the jacking notch, then crank the jack handle to lift the car until the flat tyre is 2-3 inches off the ground.
6. Fully unscrew and remove the lug nuts, then pull the flat tyre off.
7. Mount the spare wheel onto the hub bolts and hand-tighten the lug nuts clockwise.
8. Lower the jack until the tyre touches the ground, then tighten the lug nuts firmly in a criss-cross (star) pattern with the spanner.
9. Check tyre pressure (recommended: 32-33 psi) at the earliest fuel station.

simple_explanation: Engine oil keeps your engine lubricated and running cool. Checking it once a month takes just 2 minutes and prevents major engine damage.
step_by_step: 1. Park on level ground and wait 10 minutes after turning off the engine so oil settles in the oil pan.
2. Open the bonnet and locate the bright yellow dipstick handle in the engine bay.
3. Pull the dipstick out, wipe the tip completely clean with a paper towel or clean cloth.
4. Push the dipstick all the way back into the tube, then pull it out again.
5. Look at the oil level on the tip: it should be between the MIN and MAX markers. If it is near or below MIN, you need to add oil.
6. Unscrew the oil filler cap (with oil can symbol), pour 0.5 liters of recommended 5W-30 synthetic engine oil using a funnel, wait 2 minutes, and re-check with the dipstick.

simple_explanation: Coolant keeps the engine from overheating in summer and freezing in winter. Always check the clear coolant reservoir tank when the engine is COLD.
step_by_step: 1. SAFETY WARNING: NEVER open the coolant reservoir or radiator cap when the engine is hot. Boiling steam can cause severe burns.
2. Look through the translucent coolant tank beside the engine: the fluid level should be between MIN and MAX.
3. If low, wait until the engine is completely cold to the touch.
4. Slowly unscrew the expansion tank cap to release any residual pressure.
5. Top up with a 50/50 premixed ethylene glycol automotive coolant until it reaches the MAX line.
6. Screw the cap back on tightly until it clicks.

simple_explanation: The check engine light looks like a little engine silhouette on your dashboard. It tells you that the car's computer detected an issue with sensors or emissions.
step_by_step: 1. Steady / Solid Light: The computer noticed a sensor or emissions anomaly (like an oxygen sensor, loose fuel cap, or minor misfire). The car is driveable, but drive gently and schedule a scan at a service center.
2. Check Fuel Cap: A loose petrol cap is the #1 cause of false check engine lights. Tighten it until it clicks 3 times.

3. Flashing / Blinking Light: DANGER. A flashing check engine light indicates an active severe engine misfire that can melt the catalytic converter. Pull over safely immediately and turn off the engine. Call roadside assistance.
4. VehicleGPT Scan: Ask me 'What active fault codes are present?' and I will read the exact diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) from the car's CAN bus.

simple_explanation: Fuses protect electrical parts (like headlights, horn, infotainment screen, and power windows) from burning out if there is a power surge.
step_by_step: 1. Turn off the ignition and headlights.
2. Locate the fuse boxes: Cabin fuse box is beneath the driver dashboard on the right. Engine bay fuse box is on the left side beside the 12V battery.
3. Open the fuse cover and check the diagram printed on the inside of the lid to find the fuse number (e.g., F12 Horn, F24 Screen).
4. Use the small white plastic fuse puller clip inside the box to pull the fuse straight out.
5. Look at the metal wire inside the fuse: if the wire is broken or charred black, the fuse is blown.
6. Replace it with a spare fuse of the EXACT same color and amperage rating (e.g. Red = 10A, Blue = 15A, Yellow = 20A).

simple_explanation: Keeping up with routine servicing ensures your Tata Punch stays reliable, delivers maximum fuel economy, and preserves your warranty.
step_by_step: 1. 1st Service: 1,000 to 2,000 km or 2 months (Free safety check, fluid levels inspection, bolt torquing).
2. 2nd Service: 7,500 km or 6 months (General inspection, wash, tyre rotation, air filter cleaning).
3. 3rd Service: 15,000 km or 1 year (Full service: engine oil and oil filter replacement, AC cabin filter replacement).
4. Subsequent Services: Every 15,000 km or 12 months thereafter.
5. Brake Fluid & Coolant: Replace every 2 years or 30,000 km.
6. Spark Plugs: Replace every 45,000 km for smooth ignition.
